title: Sector cells divide anticlinally only between 62½° and 90°, otherwise periclinally

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sector cells divide anticlinally only between 62½° and 90°, otherwise periclinally

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: A sector-shaped (triangular) cell is likely to divide by an anticlinal wall only when its angle of arc lies between about 62½° and 90°; narrower, more tapering cells divide by a periclinal wall, which then has the smaller area.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: sector cell divides anticlinally iff 62\tfrac{1}{2}^\circ \lesssim \theta \le 90^\circ, otherwise periclinally

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We see from this, then, that what we have called an anticlinal partition, as _MP_, is only likely to occur in a triangular or prismatic cell whose angle of arc lies between 90° and 62½°. In all narrower or more tapering cells, the periclinal partition will be of less area, and will therefore be more and more likely to occur.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Anticlinal versus periclinal partitions”. Scope: wedge-shaped cells in flattened discs, growing points and embryos of plants and flattened eggs

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: sector cell divides anticlinally iff 62\tfrac{1}{2}^\circ \lesssim \theta \le 90^\circ, otherwise periclinally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The angular interval and binary wall orientation form a direct test. Open imaging permits retrospective analysis in selected tissues, but coverage around the threshold and across the full scope is limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure sector angle before division and classify the new wall as anticlinal or periclinal, testing for a transition between 62.5 and 90 degrees and comparing actual wall areas.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Tissue stress and polarity can override area minimization.

Few archives annotate pre-division sector angle.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The angular window is a sharp, refutable prediction, and some wedge-shaped cells in public apex and embryo volumes can be scored for wall orientation. Those cells are an imperfect match to the circular-sector geometry used to derive 62.5 degrees. The test is informative for growing points that have been segmented and incomplete for the wider scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure the apical angle of sector-shaped cells and whether the next wall is anticlinal or periclinal. Anticlinal walls concentrated between about 62.5 and 90 degrees, and periclinal walls in narrower sectors, would support the claim; anticlinal walls common in narrow sectors would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Meristem surface cells are polygonal prisms more often than the flat circular sectors the threshold was derived for.

Flattened discs and fern apices in the stated scope are mostly uncompiled.
